title: How to use ipfs to store text files.
description: Learn how to use ipfs to store text files.
tags: [ipfs, text, files]
categories: [ipfs, text, files]
---

In recent times, InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) has emerged as a promising repository to host files. However, the IPFS protocol is more suited for binary and large files. If you are looking to use it to store text files, there are some specific methods to do so.

Here are steps to help you to use IPFS to store text files:

1. Firstly, you need to install the IPFS in your local machine. If you are using a Unix-based system, these commands will work:

```bash
# Update package lists
sudo apt update

# Install necessary tools
sudo apt install git

# Clone the IPFS repo from its official GitHub page
git clone https://github.com/ipfs/go-ipfs

# Change directory to the go-ipfs directory
cd go-ipfs

# Build and install IPFS
make install
```

If you are using macOS, you can use Homebrew (a package manager for MacOS) to install IPFS simply via the command `brew install ipfs`.

2. Once IPFS is installed, you can initialize it with this command: `ipfs init`. This will create a new IPFS node on your machine.

3. Now, you’re ready to add your text file to the IPFS:

```bash
# Add a text file named "test.txt" to IPFS
ipfs add test.txt
```

4. Once you run the command, IPFS will add the file to its network, and give you a hash. This is the name of the directory in which IPFS stored the text file, and you can share it, not the file itself.

5. Everyone can use the hash to access the file by running:

```bash
# Fetch file
ipfs cat <hash> > downloaded.txt
```

Remember, the hash is unique to the exact content of the file. If you want to retrieve the file later, you will need the correct hash. If the file changes, a new hash is generated, and the old one is forgotten.

In this way, you can use IPFS to store text files, even though it's more suited for binary files.

(**Note:** Be careful while sharing the hashes, as anyone can then download the file from your machine.)

Use the commands as per your platform to install and run the IPFS. Also, remember to replace `<hash>` with the actual hash value you got after adding the text file.

(**Disclaimer:** IPFS is a new technology, and security and privacy implications should be carefully considered when working with it.)
